95def _prune_incompatible_python_site_paths(paths):
96 """!
97 @brief Remove site-package paths for a different Python major/minor version.
98 @param[in] paths Candidate sys.path entries.
99 @return Filtered path list.
100 """
101 current = (sys.version_info[0], sys.version_info[1])
102 pattern = re.compile(r"python(?:-)?(\d+)\.(\d+)", re.IGNORECASE)
103 filtered = []
104 for path in paths:
105 text = str(path)
106 match = pattern.search(text)
107 if match:
108 path_version = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
109 if path_version != current and ("site-packages" in text or "dist-packages" in text):
110 continue
111 filtered.append(path)
112 return filtered
113

115def _drop_imported_package(package_name: str):
116 """!
117 @brief Remove a failed/partial import package tree from sys.modules.
118 @param[in] package_name Top-level package name.
119 """
120 prefix = package_name + "."
121 for module_name in list(sys.modules):
122 if module_name == package_name or module_name.startswith(prefix):
123 sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)

126def require_numpy():
127 """!
128 @brief Import NumPy only for commands that need numeric reductions.
129 @return Imported NumPy module.
130 """
131 global _NUMPY_MODULE
132 if _NUMPY_MODULE is not None:
133 return _NUMPY_MODULE
134 try:
135 import numpy
136 except Exception as exc:
137 first_error = exc
138 original_path = list(sys.path)
139 try:
140 _drop_imported_package("numpy")
141 sys.path = _prune_incompatible_python_site_paths(original_path)
142 import numpy
143 except Exception as retry_exc:
144 raise RuntimeError(
145 "NumPy is required for this operation, but no compatible NumPy "
146 "could be imported for this Python interpreter. PICurv ignored "
147 "site-packages paths for other Python versions and retried. "
148 f"First error: {first_error}. Retry error: {retry_exc}"
149 ) from retry_exc
150 finally:
151 sys.path = original_path
152 _NUMPY_MODULE = numpy
153 return _NUMPY_MODULE

218def _source_build_identity(release_version: str) -> dict:
219 """!
220 @brief Resolve reproducible release, commit, and dirty-tree build identity.
221 @param[in] release_version Release version read from VERSION.
222 @return Mapping suitable for manifests and user-facing status output.
223 """
224 identity = {
225 "release_version": release_version,
226 "version": release_version,
227 "git_commit": None,
228 "git_short_commit": None,
229 "dirty": None,
230 "build_id": release_version,
231 }
232 try:
233 commit_result = subprocess.run(
234 ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=PACKAGE_PROJECT_ROOT,
235 text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
236 )
237 dirty_result = subprocess.run(
238 ["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"],
239 cwd=PACKAGE_PROJECT_ROOT, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
240 )
241 if commit_result.returncode == 0:
242 commit = commit_result.stdout.strip()
243 identity["git_commit"] = commit
244 identity["git_short_commit"] = commit[:12]
245 if dirty_result.returncode == 0:
246 identity["dirty"] = bool(dirty_result.stdout.strip())
247 except OSError:
248 pass
249 # Commits since the release tag, so a development build is visibly ahead of the
250 # release it names rather than claiming to be that release.
251 identity["dev_distance"] = None
252 identity["released"] = False
253 try:
254 tag_result = subprocess.run(
255 ["git", "describe", "--tags", "--match", f"v{release_version}", "--long"],
256 cwd=PACKAGE_PROJECT_ROOT, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
257 )
258 if tag_result.returncode == 0:
259 parts = tag_result.stdout.strip().rsplit("-", 2)
260 if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1].isdigit():
261 identity["dev_distance"] = int(parts[1])
262 else:
263 # No tag for this release yet: every commit is development toward it.
264 count_result = subprocess.run(
265 ["git", "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD"], cwd=PACKAGE_PROJECT_ROOT,
266 text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
267 )
268 if count_result.returncode == 0 and count_result.stdout.strip().isdigit():
269 identity["dev_distance"] = int(count_result.stdout.strip())
270 except OSError:
271 pass
272 identity["released"] = identity["dev_distance"] == 0 and not identity["dirty"]
273 if identity["git_short_commit"]:
274 development = "" if identity["dev_distance"] in (0, None) else f".dev{identity['dev_distance']}"

514 """!
515 @brief Enforce an optional workspace policy demanding a clean, released build.
516
517 @details Exploratory work should stay frictionless, so this is opt-in: a workspace
518 running a campaign that will be published sets it once, and PICurv then
519 refuses to stage from a modified or untagged tree instead of recording the
520 compromise in a manifest nobody reads until later.
521 @param[in] workspace_root Initialized workspace directory, or None.
522 @return The resolved policy mapping, empty when none is configured.
523 @throws ValueError when the active build does not satisfy the configured policy.

526 return {}

528 policy = payload.get("reproducibility") or {}
529 if not isinstance(policy, dict) or not policy:
530 return {}

532 problems = []
533 if PICURV_BUILD.get("dirty"):
534 problems.append("the source tree has uncommitted changes")
535 if PICURV_BUILD.get("dev_distance"):
536 problems.append(

538 f"v{PICURV_RELEASE_VERSION} release tag"

545 f"but this build is {PICURV_BUILD['build_id']}: " + "; ".join(problems) + ".\n"
546 "Commit and tag the release, or clear the policy for exploratory work."
547 )
548 if policy.get("pin_executables"):
549 stale = [
550 name for name, identity in sorted(runtime_build_identities().items())
551 if identity.get("available") and not identity.get("matches_source")
552 ]
553 unavailable = [
554 name for name, identity in sorted(runtime_build_identities().items())
555 if not identity.get("available")
556 ]

558 detail = []
559 if stale:
560 detail.append("built from another revision: " + ", ".join(stale))
561 if unavailable:
562 detail.append("no build identity available: " + ", ".join(unavailable))
563 raise ValueError(
564 f"{WORKSPACE_CONFIG_FILENAME} sets reproducibility.pin_executables, but "
565 "the executables do not match the active source (" + "; ".join(detail) + ").\n"

567 )

571def resolve_workspace_path(anchor_file: str, candidate: str, *, allow_external: bool = False) -> str:
572 """!
573 @brief Resolve a user path against its workspace and reject implicit escapes.
574 @param[in] anchor_file Config file whose workspace owns the reference.
575 @param[in] candidate Workspace-relative path text.
576 @param[in] allow_external Whether an explicit import/reference operation permits an absolute path.
577 @return Absolute resolved path.
578 """
579 if not isinstance(candidate, str) or not candidate.strip():
580 raise ValueError("Referenced path must be a non-empty string.")
581 text = os.path.expanduser(candidate.strip())
582 workspace_root = find_workspace_root(anchor_file)
583 if not workspace_root:
584 return os.path.abspath(text if os.path.isabs(text) else os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(anchor_file)), text))
585 if os.path.isabs(text):
586 if allow_external:
587 return os.path.abspath(text)
588 raise ValueError(
589 f"{anchor_file}: absolute path {candidate!r} is not allowed in workspace configuration; "
590 "import it with 'picurv inputs import' or use an explicit reference-mode import."
591 )
592 resolved = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(workspace_root, text))
593 if os.path.commonpath([workspace_root, resolved]) != os.path.abspath(workspace_root):
594 raise ValueError(
595 f"{anchor_file}: path {candidate!r} escapes the workspace; parent traversal is not allowed."
596 )
597 if resolved.endswith(".reference.yml") and os.path.isfile(resolved):
598 pointer = read_yaml_file(resolved)
599 external = pointer.get("picurv_external_reference") if isinstance(pointer, dict) else None
600 if not isinstance(external, str) or not os.path.isabs(external):
601 raise ValueError(f"Invalid external-reference descriptor: {resolved}")
602 if not os.path.isfile(external):
603 raise ValueError(f"Registered external input is unavailable: {external}")
604 return external
605 return resolved

◆ validate_run_directory_structure()

tuple picurv_cli.core.validate_run_directory_structure ( str  run_dir)

Refuse a run whose root has grown a directory the layout does not define.

The run topology is a contract: manifest.json publishes it, the solver's reserved-directory guard defends it, and storage classifies against it. A directory beside output/ breaks all three at once - it is routed by nothing, classified as unclassified, and therefore archived forever and pruned never. Catching it when the run is staged or resumed is the only point where the answer is still "move it", rather than "it is already in every archive of this run".

Unexpected files are reported and allowed. A stray note at a run root costs nothing and refusing to resume a long campaign over one would be a worse failure than the one being prevented.

Parameters
[in]run_dirRun root to check.
Returns
Tuple of (errors, warnings) as human-readable message lists.

666def validate_run_directory_structure(run_dir: str) -> tuple:
667 """!
668 @brief Refuse a run whose root has grown a directory the layout does not define.
669
670 @details The run topology is a contract: `manifest.json` publishes it, the solver's
671 reserved-directory guard defends it, and storage classifies against it. A
672 directory beside `output/` breaks all three at once - it is routed by
673 nothing, classified as `unclassified`, and therefore archived forever and
674 pruned never. Catching it when the run is staged or resumed is the only
675 point where the answer is still "move it", rather than "it is already in
676 every archive of this run".
677
678 Unexpected *files* are reported and allowed. A stray note at a run root
679 costs nothing and refusing to resume a long campaign over one would be a
680 worse failure than the one being prevented.
681 @param[in] run_dir Run root to check.
682 @return Tuple of (errors, warnings) as human-readable message lists.
683 """
684 root = os.path.abspath(run_dir)
685 if not os.path.isdir(root):
686 return [], []
687 allowed_files = set(RUN_ROOT_ALLOWED_FILES) | {
688 STORAGE_STATE_FILENAME, STORAGE_LOCK_FILENAME,
689 }
690 errors, warnings = [], []
691 for name in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
692 path = os.path.join(root, name)
693 if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
694 if name not in RUN_DIRECTORY_ROOTS:
695 errors.append(
696 f"{run_dir}: '{name}/' is not part of the run layout. Scientific "
697 f"output belongs under {CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['checkpoints']}, "
698 f"{CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['analysis']}, or "
699 f"{CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['visualization']}; move or remove '{name}/' "
700 f"before running. Run-owned roots are: "
701 + ", ".join(sorted(RUN_DIRECTORY_ROOTS)) + "."
702 )
703 elif name not in allowed_files:
704 warnings.append(
705 f"{run_dir}: unexpected file '{name}' at the run root. It is archived "
706 "as unclassified and never pruned."
707 )
708 return errors, warnings

751def allocate_generated_run_id(runs_root: str, case_cfg: dict, case_path: str) -> str:
752 """!
753 @brief Build the generated run identity, disambiguating a same-second collision.
754
755 @details The identity is `<run label>_<timestamp>` at one-second resolution, so two
756 runs of the same case launched back to back - a script, or a smoke
757 sequence - would otherwise name the same directory. Creating a run never
758 writes into an existing one, so the identity is advanced instead of the
759 launch being refused for a clock artifact.
760 @param[in] runs_root Directory generated runs are created beneath.
761 @param[in] case_cfg Parsed case configuration supplying the run label.
762 @param[in] case_path Case path, for the label's fallback.
763 @return Run identity that does not currently exist under `runs_root`.
764 """
765 base = f"{case_run_label(case_cfg, case_path)}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
766 run_id, suffix = base, 1
767 while os.path.exists(os.path.join(runs_root, run_id)):
768 suffix += 1
769 run_id = f"{base}-{suffix}"
770 return run_id

851 @brief Best-effort record of the PETSc, MPI, and compiler the binaries were built on.
852 @return Mapping of what could be determined; absent keys mean it could not be read.

854 identity = {}

857 identity["petsc_dir"] = petsc_dir

861 numbers = {}
862 for line in stream:
863 match = re.match(
864 r"#define\s+PETSC_VERSION_(MAJOR|MINOR|SUBMINOR)\s+(\d+)", line
865 )
866 if match:
867 numbers[match.group(1)] = match.group(2)
868 if len(numbers) == 3:
869 identity["petsc_version"] = (
870 f"{numbers['MAJOR']}.{numbers['MINOR']}.{numbers['SUBMINOR']}"
871 )
872 except OSError:
873 pass
874 if os.environ.get("PETSC_ARCH"):
875 identity["petsc_arch"] = os.environ["PETSC_ARCH"]
876 for tool, key in (("mpiexec", "mpi"), ("mpicc", "compiler")):
877 executable = shutil.which(tool)
878 if not executable:
879 continue
880 try:
881 result = subprocess.run(
882 [executable, "--version"], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=20, check=False
883 )
884 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
885 continue
886 first = (result.stdout or result.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()
887 if first:
888 identity[key] = first[0][:200]
889 return identity

1460def read_binary_build_identity(executable_path: str) -> dict:
1461 """!
1462 @brief Read the build identity a native executable was compiled with.
1463
1464 @details The Makefile stamps the release, commit, and dirty state into the
1465 binaries, and they are written into every checkpoint manifest. Reading it
1466 back is what makes the run manifest's provenance a statement about the
1467 binary that ran rather than about whatever source happens to be checked
1468 out when the conductor is invoked.
1469 @param[in] executable_path Path to `simulator` or `postprocessor`.
1470 @return Identity mapping, or an `available: False` mapping when it cannot be read.
1471 """
1472 if not os.path.isfile(executable_path) or not os.access(executable_path, os.X_OK):
1473 return {"available": False, "reason": "not built", "path": executable_path}
1474 try:
1475 result = subprocess.run(
1476 [executable_path, "--version"], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=30,
1477 )
1478 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
1479 return {"available": False, "reason": str(exc), "path": executable_path}
1480 match = _BINARY_VERSION_PATTERN.match((result.stdout or "").strip())
1481 if not match:
1482 # A binary from before the identity flag existed, or a wrapper that prints
1483 # something else. Recorded as unavailable rather than guessed at.
1484 return {"available": False, "reason": "no build identity reported",
1485 "path": executable_path}
1486 return {
1487 "available": True,
1488 "path": executable_path,
1489 "release_version": match.group("release"),
1490 "git_commit": match.group("commit"),
1491 "dirty": bool(match.group("dirty")),
1492 "build_id": (
1493 f"{match.group('release')}+g{match.group('commit')}"
1494 f"{'.dirty' if match.group('dirty') else ''}"
1495 ),
1496 }

1519def build_identity_problems(identities: dict, workspace_requirement=None) -> list:
1520 """!
1521 @brief Report every reason the active build identity is not internally coherent.
1522
1523 @details The conductor, the simulator, and the postprocessor are three artifacts
1524 that must agree before a run's provenance means anything. This states the
1525 disagreements rather than printing them, so `version status` can exit on
1526 them while ordinary staging only warns.
1527 @param[in] identities Mapping returned by `runtime_build_identities()`.
1528 @param[in] workspace_requirement Optional `software.picurv` constraint to check.
1529 @return Human-readable problem descriptions; empty when the build is coherent.
1530 """
1531 problems = []
1532 for name, identity in sorted(identities.items()):
1533 if not identity.get("available"):
1534 problems.append(
1535 f"{name}: no build identity available ({identity.get('reason', 'unknown')}); "
1536 "rebuild with 'make all'."
1537 )
1538 elif not identity.get("matches_source"):
1539 problems.append(
1540 f"{name}: built from {identity['build_id']}, but the active source is "
1541 f"{PICURV_BUILD['build_id']}; rebuild with 'make all'."
1542 )
1543 if workspace_requirement not in (None, ""):
1544 try:
1545 from packaging.specifiers import SpecifierSet
1546 from packaging.version import Version
1547 requirement_text = str(workspace_requirement).strip()
1548 if not any(token in requirement_text for token in "<>=!~"):
1549 requirement_text = "==" + requirement_text
1550 satisfied = Version(PICURV_RELEASE_VERSION) in SpecifierSet(requirement_text)
1551 except Exception:
1552 problems.append(
1553 f"workspace: software.picurv={workspace_requirement!r} is not a valid "
1554 "version or version range."
1555 )
1556 else:
1557 if not satisfied:
1558 problems.append(
1559 f"workspace: requires PICurv {workspace_requirement!r}, but the active "
1560 f"release is {PICURV_RELEASE_VERSION}."
1561 )
1562 return problems

1666def _split_error_file_and_message(raw_error: str):
1667 """!
1668 @brief Separate a validation error into its source-file and message fields when possible.
1669 @param[in] raw_error Validation error text, optionally beginning with a file path and colon.
1670 @return A pair containing the detected file path (or ``-``) and the message text.

1672 text = str(raw_error).strip()

1674 if not match:
1675 return "-", text

1678 known_suffixes = (".yml", ".yaml", ".cfg", ".picgrid", ".control", ".run", ".txt")
1679 if "/" in file_candidate or file_candidate.endswith(known_suffixes):
1680 return file_candidate, msg
1681 return "-", text

2020def _normalize_execution_override_section(payload: dict, section_name: str, config_path: str, config_label: str) -> dict:
2021 """!
2022 @brief Validate one execution override section while preserving missing-vs-empty semantics.
2023 @param[in] payload Argument passed to `_normalize_execution_override_section()`.
2024 @param[in] section_name Argument passed to `_normalize_execution_override_section()`.
2025 @param[in] config_path Argument passed to `_normalize_execution_override_section()`.
2026 @param[in] config_label Argument passed to `_normalize_execution_override_section()`.
2027 @return Value returned by `_normalize_execution_override_section()`.
2028 """
2029 section = payload.get(section_name)
2030 if section is None:
2031 return {"launcher": None, "launcher_args": None}
2032 if not isinstance(section, dict):
2033 raise ValueError(f"{config_label} at {config_path}: {section_name} must be a mapping.")
2034
2035 launcher = section.get("launcher")
2036 if launcher is not None and not isinstance(launcher, str):
2037 raise ValueError(f"{config_label} at {config_path}: {section_name}.launcher must be a string.")
2038
2039 launcher_args = None
2040 if "launcher_args" in section:
2041 launcher_args = section.get("launcher_args", [])
2042 if launcher_args is None:
2043 launcher_args = []
2044 if not isinstance(launcher_args, list):
2045 raise ValueError(f"{config_label} at {config_path}: {section_name}.launcher_args must be a list.")
2046 for i, token in enumerate(launcher_args):
2047 if not isinstance(token, (str, int, float)):
2048 raise ValueError(
2049 f"{config_label} at {config_path}: {section_name}.launcher_args[{i}] "
2050 "must be a scalar CLI token."
2051 )

2053 raise ValueError(
2054 f"{config_label} at {config_path}: {section_name}.launcher_args[{i}] "
2055 "must be a single CLI token; split whitespace-separated arguments into separate list items."
2056 )
2057 launcher_args = [str(x) for x in launcher_args]
2058
2059 return {
2060 "launcher": launcher,
2061 "launcher_args": launcher_args,
2062 }

2978def normalize_post_spectra_config(post_cfg: dict) -> dict:
2979 """!
2980 @brief Validate and canonicalize the spectra block of post.yml.
2981
2982 @details The recipe chooses what to measure; whether the case *can* support that
2983 measurement is a separate question answered by
2984 `validate_post_spectra_preconditions()`, which needs the grid and the
2985 boundary conditions. Keeping the two apart means a recipe stays valid on
2986 its own terms even when it is read without a case beside it.
2987

2990 @throws ValueError on a malformed or inconsistent recipe.
2991 """

2994 return {"output_prefix": "Spectrum", "tasks": []}
2995 if not isinstance(raw, dict):
2996 raise ValueError("'spectra' must be a mapping.")
2997

2999 if not isinstance(prefix, str) or not prefix.strip():
3000 raise ValueError("'spectra.output_prefix' must be a non-empty string.")
3001

3003 if not isinstance(tasks, list) or not tasks:
3004 raise ValueError("'spectra.tasks' must be a non-empty list.")

3009 if not isinstance(entry, dict):
3010 raise ValueError(f"spectra task {position}: each task must be a mapping.")
3011 name = entry.get("task")
3012 if name not in POST_SPECTRA_TASKS:
3013 raise ValueError(
3014 f"spectra task {position}: unknown task {name!r}. "
3015 f"Available tasks: {sorted(POST_SPECTRA_TASKS)}."
3016 )
3017 spec = POST_SPECTRA_TASKS[name]
3018
3019 field = entry.get("field", spec["fields"][0])
3020 if field not in spec["fields"]:
3021 raise ValueError(
3022 f"spectra task '{name}': field {field!r} is not supported. "
3023 f"Supported fields: {list(spec['fields'])}."
3024 )
3025
3026 block = entry.get("block", 0)
3027 if not isinstance(block, int) or isinstance(block, bool) or block < 0:
3028 raise ValueError(f"spectra task '{name}': 'block' must be a non-negative integer.")
3029
3030 symbol = entry.get("symbol", "continuum")
3031 if symbol not in POST_SPECTRA_SYMBOLS:
3032 raise ValueError(
3033 f"spectra task '{name}': unknown symbol {symbol!r}. "
3034 f"Available symbols: {list(POST_SPECTRA_SYMBOLS)}."
3035 )
3036
3037 subtract_mean = entry.get("subtract_mean", "none")
3038 if not isinstance(subtract_mean, str) or not subtract_mean.strip():
3039 raise ValueError(f"spectra task '{name}': 'subtract_mean' must be a string.")

3096 """!
3097 @brief Check spectra tasks against what the case can actually support.
3098
3099 @details Runs before any field is read, so a case with no homogeneous direction is
3100 refused rather than yielding a curve that means nothing. Only the checks
3101 the case file can answer are made here: periodicity and block count. Grid
3102 uniformity is enforced by `generators/spectra.gen`, which reads the staged
3103 PICGRID and is the only place the real node coordinates are known.

3108 @return List of formatted error strings; empty when every task is supportable.

3112 return errors

3116 except ValueError:

3118 return errors

3123 faces = {entry.get("face") for entry in block_bcs if entry.get("type") == "PERIODIC"}

3125

3127 for task_cfg in spectra_cfg["tasks"]:
3128 spec = POST_SPECTRA_TASKS[task_cfg["task"]]
3129 label = f"spectra task '{task_cfg['task']}'"

3132 errors.append(
3133 f" {post_path}: {label} requires a single-block domain; this case has "
3134 f"{block_count} blocks."
3135 )
3136
3137 block = task_cfg["block"]
3138 if block >= block_count:
3139 errors.append(
3140 f" {post_path}: {label} targets block {block}, but the case defines "
3141 f"{block_count} block(s)."
3142 )

3150 f"PERIODIC, because a shell-averaged spectrum is only defined for a "
3151 f"triply periodic homogeneous box. Non-periodic faces: {missing}."
3152 )

Count the derived fields one window would produce for a set of outputs.

3492def _post_window_derived_field_count(window_cfg: dict, outputs: list) -> int:
3493 """!
3494 @brief Count the derived fields one window would produce for a set of outputs.
3495
3496 @details Mirrors the resolution the C derivation performs, so a recipe that would
3497 produce an empty file is refused before the run rather than after it. Each
3498 output resolves against what the window accumulated: a window keeping only
3499 first moments has no stresses, RMS, or turbulent kinetic energy to give.
3500
3501 @param[in] window_cfg Normalized window definition from monitor.yml.
3502 @param[in] outputs Requested output kinds.
3503 @return Value returned by `_post_window_derived_field_count()`.
3504 """

3506 covariances = window_cfg.get("covariances", []) or []
3507 with_second = [f for f in fields if "second" in (f.get("moments") or [])]
3508 total = 0
3509 for kind in outputs:
3510 if kind == "mean":
3511 total += len(fields)
3512 elif kind == "reynolds_stress":
3513 for entry in with_second:
3514 dof = STATISTICS_ELIGIBLE_FIELDS[entry["field"]]["components"]
3515 total += 6 if dof == 3 else 1
3516 elif kind == "rms":
3517 for entry in with_second:
3518 total += STATISTICS_ELIGIBLE_FIELDS[entry["field"]]["components"]
3519 elif kind == "tke":
3520 total += sum(1 for entry in with_second
3521 if STATISTICS_ELIGIBLE_FIELDS[entry["field"]]["components"] == 3)
3522 elif kind == "flux":
3523 total += len(covariances)
3524 return total

3685def compute_post_recipe_id(post_cfg: dict) -> str:
3686 """!
3687 @brief Compute a stable human-readable identity for one post recipe.
3688 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post configuration before runtime path injection.
3689 @return Filesystem-safe recipe identity.
3690 """
3691 normalized = copy.deepcopy(post_cfg or {})
3692 normalized.pop("_picurv_paths", None)
3693 source = normalized.get("source_data")
3694 if isinstance(source, dict):
3695 source.pop("directory", None)
3696 io = normalized.get("io")
3697 label = "post"
3698 if isinstance(io, dict):
3699 io.pop("output_directory", None)
3700 raw_label = io.get("output_filename_prefix")
3701 if isinstance(raw_label, str) and raw_label.strip():
3702 label = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", raw_label.strip()).strip("-") or "post"
3703 run_control = normalized.get("run_control")
3704 if isinstance(run_control, dict):
3705 for key in POST_RUN_CONTROL_ALIASES["start_step"] + POST_RUN_CONTROL_ALIASES["end_step"]:
3706 run_control.pop(key, None)
3707 digest = hashlib.sha256(
3708 json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
3709 ).hexdigest()[:12]
3710 return f"{label}-{digest}"

3948def _scan_post_vtk_steps(prefix_path: str, extension: str) -> "set[int]":
3949 """!
3950 @brief Collect step numbers from VTK files named with a prefix, step suffix, and extension.
3951 @param[in] prefix_path Output path prefix before the numeric step suffix.
3952 @param[in] extension VTK file extension to match without its leading dot.
3953 @return Set of step numbers represented by matching files in the prefix directory.
3954 """
3955 directory = os.path.dirname(prefix_path)
3956 if not os.path.isdir(directory):
3957 return set()
3958 basename = os.path.basename(prefix_path)
3959 pattern = re.compile(rf'^{re.escape(basename)}_(\d+)\.{re.escape(extension)}$')
3960 steps = set()
3961 for name in os.listdir(directory):
3962 match = pattern.match(name)
3963 if match:
3964 steps.add(int(match.group(1)))
3965 return steps

4682def resolve_latest_restart_run(case_cfg: dict, case_path: str, start_step: int) -> str:
4683 """!
4684 @brief Select the newest local workspace run compatible with a requested restart.
4685 @param[in] case_cfg Current case configuration.
4686 @param[in] case_path Current case path.
4687 @param[in] start_step Required committed checkpoint.
4688 @return Absolute source run directory.
4689 """
4690 workspace_root = find_workspace_root(case_path, os.getcwd())
4691 if not workspace_root:
4692 raise ValueError("--from latest requires an initialized workspace.")
4693 current_graph = build_case_asset_graph(case_cfg, case_path)
4694 current_grid = next(
4695 (item for item in current_graph.get("providers", []) if item.get("kind") == "grid"),
4696 None,
4697 )
4698 candidates = []
4699 for candidate in Path(workspace_root, "runs").iterdir():
4700 if not candidate.is_dir():
4701 continue
4702 manifest = _read_json_if_exists(str(candidate / "manifest.json")) or {}
4703 lock = read_yaml_file(str(candidate / "inputs" / "assets.lock.yml")) \
4704 if (candidate / "inputs" / "assets.lock.yml").is_file() else {}
4705 locked_grid = (lock.get("assets") or {}).get("grid")
4706 runtime_grid = (lock.get("runtime_providers") or {}).get("grid")
4707 if current_grid:
4708 recorded_hash = None
4709 if isinstance(locked_grid, dict):
4710 recorded_hash = locked_grid.get("provider_spec_sha256")
4711 elif isinstance(runtime_grid, dict):
4712 recorded_hash = runtime_grid.get("provider_spec_sha256")
4713 if recorded_hash and recorded_hash != current_grid.get("spec_sha256"):
4714 continue
4715 output_root = candidate / CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS["output"]
4716 try:
4717 validate_committed_checkpoint(str(output_root), start_step)
4718 except (OSError, ValueError):
4719 continue
4720 ordering = manifest.get("updated_at") or manifest.get("created_at") or ""
4721 candidates.append((ordering, candidate.stat().st_mtime_ns, str(candidate)))
4722 if not candidates:
4723 raise ValueError(
4724 f"No local workspace run has a compatible committed checkpoint at step {start_step}. "
4725 "Restore a run from storage first, or name one explicitly with --from <run-dir>."
4726 )
4727 candidates.sort(reverse=True)
4728 selected = candidates[0][2]
4729 print(f"[INFO] Selected latest compatible restart run: {os.path.relpath(selected, workspace_root)}")
4730 return selected

5114def validate_and_nondimensionalize_picgrid(source_grid: str, dest_grid: str, L_ref: float, expected_nblk: int = None) -> dict:
5115 """!
5116 @brief Validates PICGRID payload and writes a non-dimensionalized copy.
5117 @details Requires canonical PICGRID input with leading "PICGRID" token.
5118 Output is always written in canonical PICGRID format with header and per-block dims.
5119 @param[in] source_grid Input grid file path.
5120 @param[in] dest_grid Output grid file path.
5121 @param[in] L_ref Reference length for non-dimensionalization.
5122 @param[in] expected_nblk Optional expected block count.
5123 @return Summary dictionary with nblk, dims, and total_nodes.
5124 @throws ValueError on malformed grid.
5125 """
5126 if L_ref == 0.0:
5127 raise ValueError("length_ref must be non-zero when processing grid coordinates.")
5128 if not os.path.isfile(source_grid):
5129 raise ValueError(f"Grid file not found: {source_grid}")
5130
5131 with open(source_grid, "r") as fin:
5132 line_iter = _iter_nonempty_noncomment_lines(fin)
5133 try:
5134 _, first_token = next(line_iter)
5135 except StopIteration:
5136 raise ValueError(f"Grid file '{source_grid}' is empty.")
5137
5138 if first_token != "PICGRID":
5139 raise ValueError(
5140 f"Grid file '{source_grid}' must begin with the canonical PICGRID header token."
5141 )
5142 try:
5143 _, nblk_line = next(line_iter)
5144 except StopIteration:
5145 raise ValueError(f"Grid file '{source_grid}' missing block count after PICGRID header.")
5146
5147 try:
5148 nblk = int(nblk_line)
5149 except ValueError:
5150 raise ValueError(f"Invalid block count '{nblk_line}' in grid file '{source_grid}'.")
5151 if nblk <= 0:
5152 raise ValueError(f"Grid file '{source_grid}' has non-positive block count: {nblk}.")
5153 if expected_nblk is not None and nblk != expected_nblk:
5154 raise ValueError(
5155 f"Grid file block count mismatch: case expects {expected_nblk}, grid contains {nblk}."
5156 )
5157
5158 dims = []
5159 for bi in range(nblk):
5160 try:
5161 lineno, dim_line = next(line_iter)
5162 except StopIteration:
5163 raise ValueError(f"Grid file '{source_grid}' missing dimensions for block {bi}.")
5164 parts = dim_line.split()
5165 if len(parts) != 3:
5166 raise ValueError(
5167 f"Invalid dimensions line at {source_grid}:{lineno}. Expected 3 integers, got: '{dim_line}'."
5168 )
5169 try:
5170 im, jm, km = (int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2]))
5171 except ValueError:
5172 raise ValueError(
5173 f"Invalid dimensions line at {source_grid}:{lineno}. Non-integer values: '{dim_line}'."
5174 )
5175 if im <= 0 or jm <= 0 or km <= 0:
5176 raise ValueError(
5177 f"Invalid block dimensions at {source_grid}:{lineno}: ({im}, {jm}, {km}). Must be > 0."
5178 )
5179 dims.append((im, jm, km))
5180
5181 total_nodes_expected = sum(im * jm * km for (im, jm, km) in dims)
5182 os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest_grid), exist_ok=True)
5183 with open(dest_grid, "w") as fout:
5184 fout.write("PICGRID\n")
5185 fout.write(f"{nblk}\n")
5186 for (im, jm, km) in dims:
5187 fout.write(f"{im} {jm} {km}\n")
5188
5189 total_nodes_seen = 0
5190 for lineno, coord_line in line_iter:
5191 parts = coord_line.split()
5192 if len(parts) != 3:
5193 raise ValueError(
5194 f"Invalid coordinate row at {source_grid}:{lineno}. Expected 3 floats, got: '{coord_line}'."
5195 )
5196 try:
5197 x = float(parts[0]) / L_ref
5198 y = float(parts[1]) / L_ref
5199 z = float(parts[2]) / L_ref
5200 except ValueError:
5201 raise ValueError(
5202 f"Invalid coordinate row at {source_grid}:{lineno}. Non-numeric values: '{coord_line}'."
5203 )
5204 total_nodes_seen += 1
5205 if total_nodes_seen > total_nodes_expected:
5206 raise ValueError(
5207 f"Grid file '{source_grid}' has more coordinates ({total_nodes_seen}) than expected ({total_nodes_expected})."
5208 )
5209 fout.write(
5210 f"{format_picgrid_coordinate(x)} {format_picgrid_coordinate(y)} "
5211 f"{format_picgrid_coordinate(z)}\n"
5212 )
5213
5214 if total_nodes_seen != total_nodes_expected:
5215 raise ValueError(
5216 f"Grid file '{source_grid}' has {total_nodes_seen} coordinates, expected {total_nodes_expected} from header."
5217 )
5218
5219 return {"nblk": nblk, "dims": dims, "total_nodes": total_nodes_expected}

5703def _resolve_case_relative_path(path_value: str, case_dir: str) -> str:
5704 """!
5705 @brief Resolve a path relative to the current case directory.
5706 @param[in] path_value Path from case.yml.
5707 @param[in] case_dir Current case directory.
5708 @return Absolute path.
5709 """
5710 if not isinstance(path_value, str) or not path_value.strip():
5711 raise ValueError("path value must be a non-empty string.")
5712 workspace_root = find_workspace_root(case_dir)
5713 if workspace_root:
5714 if os.path.isabs(path_value):
5715 raise ValueError(
5716 f"absolute path {path_value!r} is not allowed in workspace case configuration; "
5717 "use 'picurv inputs import --mode reference' for an explicit external reference."
5718 )
5719 resolved = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(workspace_root, path_value))
5720 if os.path.commonpath([workspace_root, resolved]) != os.path.abspath(workspace_root):
5721 raise ValueError(f"path {path_value!r} escapes the workspace.")
5722 if resolved.endswith(".reference.yml") and os.path.isfile(resolved):
5723 pointer = read_yaml_file(resolved)
5724 external = pointer.get("picurv_external_reference") if isinstance(pointer, dict) else None
5725 if not isinstance(external, str) or not os.path.isabs(external):
5726 raise ValueError(f"Invalid external-reference descriptor: {resolved}")
5727 if not os.path.isfile(external):
5728 raise ValueError(f"Registered external input is unavailable: {external}")
5729 return external
5730 return resolved
5731 if os.path.isabs(path_value):
5732 return os.path.abspath(path_value)
5733 return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(case_dir, path_value))

6174def _bc_profile_expected_dims(face: str, block_dims: tuple) -> tuple:
6175 """!
6176 @brief Return expected PICSLICE dimensions for a face and block node dimensions.

6191 return (jm - 1, im - 1)

6503def _case_reynolds_number(case_cfg: dict):
6504 """!
6505 @brief Reynolds number implied by a case's scaling and fluid properties.
6506 @param case_cfg Parsed case configuration.
6507 @return The Reynolds number, or None when the inputs are absent or unusable.
6508 """
6509 try:
6510 props = case_cfg.get('properties', {}) or {}
6511 scaling = props.get('scaling', {}) or {}
6512 fluid = props.get('fluid', {}) or {}
6513 density = float(fluid.get('density'))
6514 viscosity = float(fluid.get('viscosity'))
6515 length_ref = float(scaling.get('length_ref'))
6516 velocity_ref = float(scaling.get('velocity_ref'))
6517 except (TypeError, ValueError):
6518 return None
6519 if viscosity <= 0.0:
6520 return None
6521 return density * velocity_ref * length_ref / viscosity

7296def classify_run_directory_value(value) -> str:
7297 """!
7298 @brief Classify a configured run directory value.
7299
7300 @details Containment is judged lexically against the run directory, because the run
7301 directory does not exist yet at validation time. Beyond escaping, a value
7302 is rejected when it resolves to the run root itself: the log directory is
7303 recursively deleted on a fresh solve, so `.` or `a/..` would delete the run.
7304 @param[in] value Configured directory value from monitor `io.directories`.
7305 @return One of "contained", "escaping", "tilde", "run_root", or "invalid".
7306 """
7307 if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
7308 return "invalid"
7309 candidate = value.strip()
7310 # `~` is its own verdict because nothing expands it anywhere in the pipeline. The
7311 # control file is read by PETSc, not by a shell, and both the planner and the C
7312 # runtime treat a value not starting with `/` as relative to the run - so `~/logs`
7313 # names a literal `~` directory inside the run tree.
7314 #
7315 # It was worse before this verdict existed: physical containment classified `~` as
7316 # an authorizable external absolute location by expanding it, while every layer
7317 # that actually used the value treated it literally. The two disagreed about which
7318 # directory was being deleted. The fix is to refuse the value, not to expand it -
7319 # expanding it in one layer would only move the disagreement.
7320 if candidate.startswith("~"):
7321 return "tilde"
7322 if os.path.isabs(candidate):
7323 return "escaping"
7324 normalized = os.path.normpath(candidate)
7325 if normalized == os.pardir or normalized.startswith(os.pardir + os.sep):
7326 return "escaping"
7327 if normalized in (".", ""):
7328 return "run_root"
7329 return "contained"

7525def classify_physical_containment(run_dir: str, values: dict) -> list:
7526 """!
7527 @brief Classify where each run-owned directory physically lands.
7528
7529 @details Lexical containment is not enough: a contained name can be a symlink to an
7530 external directory, and `PetscRMTree` follows symlinks. This resolves the
7531 real path - including any symlinked ancestor - and reports a typed verdict
7532 so the caller can apply the waiver rule structurally.
7533 @param[in] run_dir Run directory the values are relative to.
7534 @param[in] values Effective directory mapping.
7535 @return List of (key, verdict, message) for every value that is not contained.
7536 """
7537 findings: list = []
7538 try:
7539 root = os.path.realpath(run_dir)
7540 except OSError:
7541 return findings
7542 for key in RUN_OWNED_DIRECTORY_KEYS:
7543 raw = values.get(key)
7544 if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
7545 continue
7546 text = raw.strip()
7547 # Whether the *value* was given as an absolute location, which is the only form
7548 # an authorization can cover. A relative name that resolves outside the tree got
7549 # there through a symlink, and that is never what an operator asked for.
7550 # Only a real absolute path can be waived. `~` is refused before this point by
7551 # the lexical rules, and is not expanded here either: an earlier version did
7552 # expand it, which made this layer reason about a home directory no other layer
7553 # ever resolves.
7554 absolute = text.startswith("/")
7555 candidate = os.path.join(run_dir, text)
7556 real = os.path.realpath(candidate)
7557
7558 if real == root:
7559 findings.append((key, PHYSICAL_VERDICT_RUN_ROOT,
7560 f"'io.directories.{key}' = {raw!r} resolves to the run directory itself "
7561 f"({real!r}); deleting it would destroy the run. This cannot be overridden."))
7562 elif real == os.sep or root.startswith(real.rstrip(os.sep) + os.sep):
7563 findings.append((key, PHYSICAL_VERDICT_ANCESTOR,
7564 f"'io.directories.{key}' = {raw!r} resolves to {real!r}, which CONTAINS the run "
7565 f"directory {root!r}. The runtime deletes this path recursively, so it would "
7566 f"destroy the run and everything beside it. This cannot be overridden."))
7567 elif real.startswith(root + os.sep):
7568 continue
7569 elif absolute:
7570 findings.append((key, PHYSICAL_VERDICT_EXTERNAL_ABSOLUTE,
7571 f"'io.directories.{key}' = {raw!r} resolves to {real!r}, which is outside the run "
7572 f"directory {root!r}. The runtime deletes its log directory recursively."))
7573 else:
7574 findings.append((key, PHYSICAL_VERDICT_RELATIVE_ESCAPE,
7575 f"'io.directories.{key}' = {raw!r} is a relative name that resolves to {real!r}, "
7576 f"outside the run directory {root!r} - a symlink leads out of the tree. A "
7577 f"relative escape is never authorizable; name an absolute path if an external "
7578 f"location is genuinely intended. This cannot be overridden."))
7579 return findings

7633def validate_reserved_directory_flags(config: dict, config_path: str, label: str) -> list:
7634 """!
7635 @brief Reject raw PETSc passthrough options that set run-owned directories.
7636
7637 @details Passthrough surfaces emit `{flag: value}` verbatim into the generated
7638 control file. Run-owned path flags are reserved for the fixed workspace
7639 topology and may only be emitted by the generator.
7640 @param[in] config Parsed configuration mapping to scan.
7641 @param[in] config_path Path to the file, for error messages.
7642 @param[in] label Human-readable description of the surface being scanned.
7643 @return Violation lines.
7644 """
7645 violations: list = []
7646
7647 def scan(node, trail: str) -> None:
7648 """!
7649 @brief Walk the mapping looking for reserved flags used as keys.
7650 @param[in] node Current mapping, list, or scalar node.
7651 @param[in] trail Dotted path to the current node, for error messages.
7652 @return None.
7653 """
7654 if isinstance(node, dict):
7655 for key, value in node.items():
7656 token = key.strip() if isinstance(key, str) else key
7657 if token in RESERVED_DIRECTORY_FLAGS:
7658 violations.append(
7659 f" {config_path}: {label} sets the reserved flag '{token}' at "
7660 f"{trail or '<root>'}. Run directories are fixed by the workspace "
7661 "contract; raw passthrough cannot override them."
7662 )
7663 elif token in RESERVED_INDIRECTION_FLAGS:
7664 violations.append(
7665 f" {config_path}: {label} sets '{token}' at {trail or '<root>'}. PETSc "
7666 f"evaluates that indirection itself, so its contents cannot be checked "
7667 "here and could reintroduce a run-directory flag. Remove the indirection."
7668 )
7669 scan(value, f"{trail}.{key}" if trail else str(key))
7670 elif isinstance(node, list):
7671 for index, item in enumerate(node):
7672 scan(item, f"{trail}[{index}]")
7673
7674 scan(config, "")
7675 return violations

Validates every configuration a simulation run consumes, before any work is done.

Covers the three roles the solver is launched with: the case, the solver, and the monitor. Only one of those is a solver configuration, which is why this is not named for the solver; the monitor in particular carries observation and field-statistics contracts that have nothing to do with the numerical scheme.

Checks required sections, required keys, physical sanity, and the cross-file combinations no single file can rule out. Post-processing configuration is validated separately by validate_post_config().

◆ check_post_checkpoint_cadence_alignment()

"tuple[list, list]" picurv_cli.core.check_post_checkpoint_cadence_alignment ( dict  post_cfg,
dict  monitor_cfg,
str  post_path,
str   monitor_path = "monitor.yml" 
)

Report post step selections that cannot land on a committed checkpoint.

The post-processor reads committed bundles, and the solver commits one every io.data_output_frequency completed steps. A step_interval that is not a multiple of that cadence therefore asks for steps that were never written: the source-frontier scan stops at the first missing one and processes far less than the recipe requested. That is only discovered after a solve has already run, so it is caught here instead.

The solver also commits the initial and final states off cadence, which is why a misaligned start_step is a warning rather than an error: it may legitimately be the run's own starting step. step_interval has no such exemption, because a stride off the cadence cannot land on two consecutive checkpoints whatever the run's bounds are.

Parameters
[in]post_cfgParsed post-processing configuration.
[in]monitor_cfgParsed monitor configuration governing the source run.
[in]post_pathPath to the post file, for error messages.
[in]monitor_pathPath to the monitor file, for error messages.
Returns
(errors, warnings), each a list of message strings. Both are empty when the comparison cannot be made, because the inputs that would make it meaningful are validated and reported elsewhere.

8470 """!
8471 @brief Report post step selections that cannot land on a committed checkpoint.
8472
8473 @details The post-processor reads committed bundles, and the solver commits one
8474 every `io.data_output_frequency` completed steps. A `step_interval` that
8475 is not a multiple of that cadence therefore asks for steps that were
8476 never written: the source-frontier scan stops at the first missing one
8477 and processes far less than the recipe requested. That is only
8478 discovered after a solve has already run, so it is caught here instead.
8479
8480 The solver also commits the initial and final states off cadence, which
8481 is why a misaligned `start_step` is a warning rather than an error: it
8482 may legitimately be the run's own starting step. `step_interval` has no
8483 such exemption, because a stride off the cadence cannot land on two
8484 consecutive checkpoints whatever the run's bounds are.
8485
8486 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post-processing configuration.
8487 @param[in] monitor_cfg Parsed monitor configuration governing the source run.
8488 @param[in] post_path Path to the post file, for error messages.
8489 @param[in] monitor_path Path to the monitor file, for error messages.
8490 @return `(errors, warnings)`, each a list of message strings. Both are empty when
8491 the comparison cannot be made, because the inputs that would make it
8492 meaningful are validated and reported elsewhere.
8493 """
8494 errors = []
8495 warnings = []
8496 if not isinstance(post_cfg, dict) or not isinstance(monitor_cfg, dict):
8497 return errors, warnings
8498
8499 io_cfg = monitor_cfg.get("io") or {}
8500 if not isinstance(io_cfg, dict):
8501 return errors, warnings
8502 try:
8503 cadence = int(io_cfg["data_output_frequency"])
8504 except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
8505 # A missing or malformed cadence is reported by the monitor's own checks.
8506 return errors, warnings
8507 # A disabled cadence commits only the initial and final states, so there is no
8508 # stride to align to.
8509 if cadence <= 0:
8510 return errors, warnings
8511
8512 try:
8513 step_interval = int(get_post_run_control_value(post_cfg, "step_interval", 1))
8514 start_step = int(get_post_run_control_value(post_cfg, "start_step", 0))
8515 except (TypeError, ValueError):
8516 # Reported by the run_control checks, which run against the same values.
8517 return errors, warnings
8518
8519 if step_interval > 0 and step_interval % cadence != 0:
8520 suggestion = max(cadence, (step_interval // cadence) * cadence)
8521 errors.append(
8522 f" {post_path}: 'run_control.step_interval' is {step_interval}, which is not a "
8523 f"multiple of 'io.data_output_frequency' ({cadence}) in {monitor_path}. The solver "
8524 f"only commits a checkpoint every {cadence} steps, so most requested steps were "
8525 f"never written and post-processing would stop at the first missing one. Use "
8526 f"{suggestion}, or another multiple of {cadence}, or lower the monitor cadence."
8527 )
8528
8529 if start_step > 0 and start_step % cadence != 0:
8530 warnings.append(
8531 f"{post_path}: 'run_control.start_step' is {start_step}, which is not a multiple of "
8532 f"'io.data_output_frequency' ({cadence}) in {monitor_path}. That step only exists if "
8533 f"it is the run's own starting step, which is committed off cadence."
8534 )
8535
8536 return errors, warnings

9145def flatten_study_parameters(parameters: dict) -> dict:
9146 """!
9147 @brief Flatten grouped study overrides into scalar dotted-path columns.
9148
9149 @details A grouped override such as `case.run_control: {dt_physical: ...}`
9150 materializes correctly in case YAML but is not a useful CSV cell or
9151 plot coordinate. Flattening preserves the actual varied variables.

9154 @return Flat dotted-path-to-scalar mapping.

9158 def visit(prefix, value):
9159 """!
9160 @brief Recursively flatten one grouped override value.
9161 @param[in] prefix Current dotted parameter path.
9162 @param[in] value Scalar or nested mapping at the current path.
9163 """
9164 if isinstance(value, dict):
9165 for child, child_value in value.items():
9166 visit(f"{prefix}.{child}" if prefix else str(child), child_value)
9167 else:
9168 flattened[prefix] = value
9169
9170 for key, value in (parameters or {}).items():
9171 visit(str(key), value)
9172 return flattened

10238 lines.append(f"{prefix}_covariance_count {len(window['covariances'])}")
10239 for pair_index, pair in enumerate(window["covariances"]):
10240 lines.append(f"{prefix}_covariance_{pair_index} {pair[0]},{pair[1]}")

10616def generate_picgrid_from_programmatic_settings(raw_settings: dict, dest_path: str, L_ref: float) -> dict:
10617 """!
10618 @brief Generate a canonical PICGRID file from programmatic Cartesian grid settings.
10619 @details Implements the same coordinate formula as ComputeStretchedCoord in src/grid.c.
10620 im/jm/km in raw_settings are cell counts; node counts are im+1, jm+1, km+1.
10621 @param[in] raw_settings programmatic_settings dict from case.yml.
10622 @param[in] dest_path Destination PICGRID file path.
10623 @param[in] L_ref Reference length for nondimensionalization (must be non-zero).
10624 @return Summary dict: nblk, dims [(IM, JM, KM)], total_nodes.
10625 """
10626 validate_programmatic_generated_ic_grid_settings(raw_settings)
10627 if L_ref == 0.0:
10628 raise ValueError("length_ref must be non-zero for programmatic grid generation.")
10629 IM = int(raw_settings.get("im", 0)) + 1
10630 JM = int(raw_settings.get("jm", 0)) + 1
10631 KM = int(raw_settings.get("km", 0)) + 1
10632 if IM < 2 or JM < 2 or KM < 2:
10633 raise ValueError(
10634 f"programmatic_settings im/jm/km must each be >= 1 "
10635 f"(got im={IM-1}, jm={JM-1}, km={KM-1})."
10636 )
10637 x_min = float(raw_settings.get("xMins", 0.0))
10638 x_max = float(raw_settings.get("xMaxs", 1.0))
10639 y_min = float(raw_settings.get("yMins", 0.0))
10640 y_max = float(raw_settings.get("yMaxs", 1.0))
10641 z_min = float(raw_settings.get("zMins", 0.0))
10642 z_max = float(raw_settings.get("zMaxs", 1.0))
10643 rx = float(raw_settings.get("rxs", 1.0))
10644 ry = float(raw_settings.get("rys", 1.0))
10645 rz = float(raw_settings.get("rzs", 1.0))
10646
10647 def _stretched(idx, N, length, r):
10648 """!
10649 @brief Mirror of ComputeStretchedCoord from src/grid.c.
10650 @param[in] idx Node index along the axis.
10651 @param[in] N Total node count along the axis.
10652 @param[in] length Physical length of the axis.
10653 @param[in] r Geometric stretching ratio.
10654 @return Coordinate offset from the axis minimum.
10655 """
10656 frac = idx / (N - 1.0)
10657 if abs(r - 1.0) < 1.0e-9:
10658 return length * frac
10659 return length * (r ** frac - 1.0) / (r - 1.0)
10660
10661 Lx, Ly, Lz = x_max - x_min, y_max - y_min, z_max - z_min
10662 os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest_path), exist_ok=True)
10663 with open(dest_path, "w") as fout:
10664 fout.write("PICGRID\n1\n")
10665 fout.write(f"{IM} {JM} {KM}\n")
10666 for k in range(KM):
10667 z = (z_min + _stretched(k, KM, Lz, rz)) / L_ref
10668 for j in range(JM):
10669 y = (y_min + _stretched(j, JM, Ly, ry)) / L_ref
10670 for i in range(IM):
10671 x = (x_min + _stretched(i, IM, Lx, rx)) / L_ref
10672 fout.write(
10673 f"{format_picgrid_coordinate(x)} {format_picgrid_coordinate(y)} "
10674 f"{format_picgrid_coordinate(z)}\n"
10675 )
10676 total_nodes = IM * JM * KM
10677 return {"nblk": 1, "dims": [(IM, JM, KM)], "total_nodes": total_nodes}

11347def validate_petsc_vec_binary(path: str) -> dict:
11348 """!
11349 @brief Validate the basic PETSc binary VecView envelope used by ReadFieldData.
11350 @param[in] path PETSc binary vector path.
11351 @return Summary containing the absolute path and scalar count.
11352 """
11353 import struct
11354 with open(path, "rb") as fin:
11355 header = fin.read(8)
11356 if len(header) != 8:
11357 raise ValueError(f"PETSc Vec file is too short: {path}")
11358 class_id, scalar_count = struct.unpack(">ii", header)
11359 if class_id != 1211214 or scalar_count < 0:
11360 raise ValueError(f"Invalid PETSc Vec header in {path}.")
11361 payload = fin.read()
11362 if len(payload) != scalar_count * 8:
11363 raise ValueError(
11364 f"PETSc Vec payload size mismatch in {path}: expected {scalar_count * 8} bytes, found {len(payload)}."
11365 )
11366 return {"path": os.path.abspath(path), "scalar_count": scalar_count}

11703def infer_unique_inlet_axis_from_prepared_bcs(prepared_blocks: list) -> "str | None":
11704 """!
11705 @brief Infer the unique inlet axis across all blocks using C-side "primary inlet" ordering.
11706 @param[in] prepared_blocks Normalized BC blocks from `validate_and_prepare_boundary_conditions`.
11707 @return One of `"x"`, `"y"`, `"z"` if unique, `None` if no inlet exists.
11708 @throws ValueError if different blocks imply different inlet axes.
11709 """
11710 face_order = ("-Xi", "+Xi", "-Eta", "+Eta", "-Zeta", "+Zeta")
11711 face_axis = {
11712 "-Xi": "x", "+Xi": "x",
11713 "-Eta": "y", "+Eta": "y",
11714 "-Zeta": "z", "+Zeta": "z",
11715 }
11716
11717 inlet_axes = set()
11718 for block_bcs in prepared_blocks:
11719 face_map = {entry["face"]: entry for entry in block_bcs}
11720 for face in face_order:
11721 entry = face_map.get(face)
11722 if entry and entry["type"] == "INLET":
11723 inlet_axes.add(face_axis[face])
11724 break
11725
11726 if not inlet_axes:
11727 return None
11728 if len(inlet_axes) != 1:
11729 raise ValueError(
11730 "properties.initial_conditions.peak_velocity_physical requires all blocks to have a primary INLET "
11731 f"on the same axis. Found axes: {sorted(inlet_axes)}. Use u_physical/v_physical/w_physical instead."
11732 )
11733 return next(iter(inlet_axes))

Guard a value that is written verbatim into the generated control file.

PETSc reads the control file line by line, so a value containing a newline writes additional option lines - which defeats every key-based check by smuggling a whole new flag. Rejecting the value is the only safe handling; there is no quoting that makes a multi-line option meaningful.

12162def control_value(value, context: str):
12163 """!
12164 @brief Guard a value that is written verbatim into the generated control file.
12165
12166 @details PETSc reads the control file line by line, so a value containing a newline
12167 writes additional option lines - which defeats every key-based check by
12168 smuggling a whole new flag. Rejecting the value is the only safe handling;
12169 there is no quoting that makes a multi-line option meaningful.
12170 @param[in] value Configured value destined for a control line.
12171 @param[in] context YAML path, for the error message.
12172 @return The value unchanged when it is safe to emit.
12173 @throws SystemExit when the value would inject an option line.
12174 """
12175 text = str(value)
12176 if any(character in text for character in ("\n", "\r")):
12177 print(
12178 f"[FATAL] {context} contains a newline. Values written to the generated control "
12179 f"file must occupy a single line; a multi-line value would inject additional "
12180 f"PETSc options.",
12181 file=sys.stderr,
12182 )
12183 sys.exit(1)
12184 return value

12187def append_passthrough_flags(control_lines: list, options: dict):
12188 """!
12189 @brief Appends raw CLI flags to the control list from a {flag: value} dict.
12190 @details Boolean `true` is emitted as a switch with no value. Boolean `false`
12191 is skipped. All other values are emitted as "<flag> <value>".
12192 @param[out] control_lines The destination list of control-file lines.
12193 @param[in] options Mapping of raw CLI flags to values.
12194 """
12195 if not options:
12196 return
12197 for flag, value in options.items():
12198 if isinstance(flag, str) and flag.strip() in RESERVED_DIRECTORY_FLAGS:
12199 # Defense in depth: validation rejects these, but the emitter must never
12200 # write a run-directory flag from an unvalidated passthrough surface.
12201 raise ValueError(
12202 f"Refusing to emit reserved directory flag '{flag.strip()}' from passthrough "
12203 "options; run directories are fixed by the workspace contract."
12204 )
12205 if isinstance(value, bool):
12206 if value:
12207 control_lines.append(str(flag))
12208 continue
12209 control_lines.append(
12210 f"{flag} {control_value(format_flag_value(value), f'passthrough option {flag}')}"

12485 """!
12486 @brief Warn when absolute_tol is set but cannot affect convergence.
12487
12488 absolute_tol bounds the velocity update. Since |dU| ~ dtau*|R|, bounding it
12489 absolutely is a disguised, step-size-dependent residual bound, so it takes no
12490 part once a residual tolerance is active -- which is now the default. Setting it
12491 therefore has no effect, and silently ineffective knobs are what this warning
12492 exists to prevent. See docs/pages/24_Dual_Time_Picard_Jameson_RK.md.
12493 @param[in] cfg Tolerance mapping to inspect for `absolute_tol` and the residual keys.
12494 @param[in] where Config path used to locate the offending key in the warning text.
12495 @return None; emits a warning on stderr when `absolute_tol` cannot take effect.

12681 def _warn_if_krylov_coarse_solver(ksp_type, source_key: str):
12682 """!
12683 @brief Warn when the coarsest multigrid level is given a Krylov solver.
12684 @param[in] ksp_type PETSc KSP token configured for `level_0`.
12685 @param[in] source_key Name of the source YAML block, used in the message.
12686 @details level_0 is the coarse solve at the base of the V-cycle, not a
12687 smoother. A Krylov method there makes the multigrid
12688 preconditioner a nonlinear operator, which decouples the outer
12689 KSP's tracked residual from the true residual b-Ax. This stays a
12690 warning rather than an error because it remains legitimate at
12691 large scale when tolerances are set against the true residual.
12692 """
12693 if str(ksp_type).strip().lower() not in KRYLOV_KSP_TYPES:
12694 return
12695 print(
12696 f"[WARNING] {source_key}.multigrid.level_solvers.level_0.method = '{ksp_type}' "
12697 "is a Krylov method. level_0 is the multigrid COARSE SOLVE, not a smoother, "
12698 "so a Krylov method there makes the preconditioner nonlinear and the outer "
12699 "KSP's tracked residual can stop matching the true residual b-Ax. "
12700 "Prefer {method: preonly, preconditioner: redundant}. If this is deliberate, "
12701 "enable solver_monitoring.poisson.pic_true_residual and set tolerances against "
12702 "the true residual. See docs/pages/25_Pressure_Poisson_GMRES_Multigrid.md.",
12703 file=sys.stderr,
12704 )
12705
12706 def _poisson_level_number(level_name) -> int:
12707 """!
12708 @brief Extract the numeric suffix from a `level_N` multigrid level key.
12709 @param[in] level_name YAML level key supplied by the user.
12710 @return Numeric level suffix.
12711 """
12712 text = str(level_name).strip()
12713 match = re.fullmatch(r"level_(\d+)", text)
12714 if not match:
12715 raise ValueError(f"Invalid Poisson multigrid level name '{level_name}'. Expected 'level_N'.")
12716 return int(match.group(1))

13175def execute_command(command: list, run_dir: str, log_filename: str, monitor_cfg: dict = None):
13176 """!
13177 @brief Executes a command, streaming its output to the console and a log file.
13178 @details ...
13179 If None, the process inherits the parent's environment directly.
13180 @param[in] command Argument passed to `execute_command()`.

13192 # --- Environment Handling ---

13194 "stdout": subprocess.PIPE, "stderr": subprocess.STDOUT,

13216 sys.stdout.write(line)

13220 print("-" * 60)

13222 print(f"[SUCCESS] Execution finished successfully.")
13223 else:
13224 print(f"[FATAL] Execution failed with exit code {return_code}. Check log: {os.path.relpath(log_path)}", file=sys.stderr)
13225 sys.exit(return_code)
13226 except FileNotFoundError:

13228 print(" Please check that the path is correct and the file has execute permissions.", file=sys.stderr)

13578 monitor_path = active.get("monitor")
13579 solver_control_path = active.get("control")

13581 return case_path, monitor_path, solver_control_path
13582 all_yml_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "*.yml"))

13593 except Exception as e:

13595 try:
13596 solver_control_path = glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "*.control"))[0]
13597 except IndexError:
13598 solver_control_path = None

13846def extract_metric_from_csv(case_dir: str, spec: dict):
13847 """!
13848 @brief Extract a scalar metric from a CSV source.
13849 @param[in] case_dir Argument passed to `extract_metric_from_csv()`.
13850 @param[in] spec Argument passed to `extract_metric_from_csv()`.
13851 @return Value returned by `extract_metric_from_csv()`.
13852 """
13853 file_glob = spec.get("file_glob", "**/*_msd.csv")
13854 candidates = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(case_dir, file_glob), recursive=True))
13855 if not candidates:
13856 return None
13857 csv_path = candidates[0]
13858 rows = []
13859 with open(csv_path, "r", newline="") as f:
13860 reader = csv.DictReader(f)
13861 if reader.fieldnames:
13862 for row in reader:
13863 rows.append(row)
13864 if not rows:
13865 return None
13866 column = spec.get("column")
13867 numerator_column = spec.get("numerator_column")
13868 denominator_column = spec.get("denominator_column")
13869 denominator_floor = float(spec.get("denominator_floor", 0.0) or 0.0)
13870 if not column and not numerator_column:
13871 for name in reversed(reader.fieldnames):
13872 if name and name.lower() not in {"step", "time", "timestep"}:
13873 column = name
13874 break
13875 if not column and not numerator_column:
13876 return None
13877 values = []
13878 for row in rows:
13879 try:
13880 if numerator_column:
13881 numerator = float(row[numerator_column])
13882 denominator = float(row[denominator_column])
13883 denominator = max(denominator_floor, denominator)
13884 if denominator == 0.0:
13885 continue
13886 values.append(numerator / denominator)
13887 else:
13888 values.append(float(row[column]))
13889 except Exception:
13890 continue
13891 else:
13892 return None
13893 return reduce_metric_values(values, spec.get("reduction", "last"))

14018 except Exception:

14245def _study_linear_y_limits(values: list) -> "tuple[float, float] | None":
14246 """!
14247 @brief Build padded linear limits that include zero for non-negative metrics.
14248 @param[in] values Finite metric values.
14249 @return Lower and upper limits, or None for an empty sequence.
14250 """
14251 if not values:
14252 return None
14253 lower, upper = min(values), max(values)
14254 if lower >= 0.0:
14255 lower = 0.0
14256 span = upper - lower
14257 padding = max(span * 0.06, abs(upper) * 0.02, 1.0e-12)
14258 return (lower, upper + padding) if lower == 0.0 else (lower - padding, upper + padding)

15156def _asset_file_sha256(path: str) -> str:
15157 """!
15158 @brief Hash an asset source or payload without loading it into memory.
15159 @param[in] path File to hash.
15160 @return Lowercase SHA-256 digest.
15161 """
15162 digest = hashlib.sha256()
15163 with open(path, "rb") as stream:
15164 for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(8 * 1024 * 1024), b""):
15165 digest.update(block)
15166 return digest.hexdigest()

15346 """!

15348 @param[in] graph Provider graph returned by build_case_asset_graph.

15350 @param[in] precomputable_only Exclude runtime-C providers for normal-run staging.

15353 by_kind = {item["kind"]: item for item in graph["providers"]}

15355 unknown = requested_set - set(by_kind)
15356 if unknown:
15357 raise ValueError(
15358 f"No configured provider exists for asset kind(s): {sorted(unknown)}. "
15359 f"Configured kinds: {sorted(by_kind)}."

15363 def add(kind):

15366 @param[in] kind Asset kind to include.

15370 return

15372 for dependency in by_kind[kind].get("dependencies", []):
15373 if dependency in by_kind:
15374 add(dependency)

15376 for kind in requested_set:

15505 @brief Read a canonical PICGRID and summarize what a user would want to check.

15520 continue

15522 point = [float(value) for value in parts]
15523 except ValueError:
15524 continue

15527 bounds[0][axis] = min(bounds[0][axis], point[axis])
15528 bounds[1][axis] = max(bounds[1][axis], point[axis])
15529 extent = [bounds[1][axis] - bounds[0][axis] for axis in range(3)] if nodes else [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
15530 return {
15531 "blocks": len(dims),
15532 "dimensions": [list(item) for item in dims],
15533 "total_nodes": nodes,
15534 "bounds_min": bounds[0] if nodes else None,
15535 "bounds_max": bounds[1] if nodes else None,
15536 "extent": extent,
15537 }

15540def _write_structured_grid_preview(picgrid_path: str, destination: str, dims) -> bool:
15541 """!
15542 @brief Write a single-block ASCII VTS preview of a staged PICGRID.
15543
15544 @details Only the first block is written: the preview exists so a user can confirm
15545 the shape they configured, not to reproduce the solver's view of a
15546 multi-block domain.
15547 @param[in] picgrid_path Staged PICGRID file.
15548 @param[in] destination Preview path to write.
15549 @param[in] dims Per-block dimension triples.
15550 @return True when a preview was written.
15551 """
15552 if not dims:
15553 return False
15554 im, jm, km = (int(value) for value in dims[0])
15555 if im * jm * km > ASSET_PREVIEW_NODE_LIMIT:
15556 return False
15557 coordinates = []
15558 with open(picgrid_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
15559 iterator = _iter_nonempty_noncomment_lines(stream)
15560 for _ in range(2 + len(dims)):
15561 next(iterator, None)
15562 for _lineno, line in iterator:
15563 parts = line.split()
15564 if len(parts) == 3:
15565 coordinates.append(line)
15566 if len(coordinates) >= im * jm * km:
15567 break
15568 if len(coordinates) < im * jm * km:
15569 return False
15570 os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(destination), exist_ok=True)
15571 with open(destination, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
15572 extent = f"0 {im - 1} 0 {jm - 1} 0 {km - 1}"
15573 out.write('<?xml version="1.0"?>\n')
15574 out.write('<VTKFile type="StructuredGrid" version="1.0" byte_order="LittleEndian">\n')
15575 out.write(f' <StructuredGrid WholeExtent="{extent}">\n')
15576 out.write(f' <Piece Extent="{extent}">\n')
15577 out.write(' <Points>\n')
15578 out.write(' <DataArray type="Float64" NumberOfComponents="3" format="ascii">\n')
15579 for row in coordinates:
15580 out.write(f" {row}\n")
15581 out.write(' </DataArray>\n </Points>\n')
15582 out.write(' </Piece>\n </StructuredGrid>\n</VTKFile>\n')
15583 return True

15748def _workspace_asset_set_name(workspace_root: str, case_path: str) -> str:
15749 """!
15750 @brief Return a collision-free, readable mutable asset-set name.
15751 @param[in] workspace_root Owning initialized workspace.

15754 """
15755 stem = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", Path(case_path).stem).strip("-") or "case"

16756def parse_case_index_tsv(tsv_path: str) -> list:
16757 """!
16758 @brief Parse a case_index.tsv file back into a list of case entry dicts.
16759 @param[in] tsv_path Path to the case_index.tsv file.
16760 @return List of dicts with keys: index, case_id, run_dir, control_file,
16761 post_recipe_file, log_level, post_prefix.
16762 """
16763 entries = []
16764 with open(tsv_path) as f:
16765 for line in f:
16766 line = line.strip()
16767 if not line:
16768 continue
16769 parts = line.split("\t")
16770 entries.append({
16771 "index": int(parts[0]),
16772 "case_id": parts[1],
16773 "run_dir": parts[2],
16774 "control_file": parts[3],
16775 "post_recipe_file": parts[4],
16776 "log_level": parts[5],
16777 "post_prefix": parts[6],
16778 })
16779 return entries
16780

17869def _parse_momentum_convergence_logs(log_dir: str) -> "tuple[dict, dict, list[int]]":

17889 r"\s*\|Rk\|/\|R0\|:\s*(?P<resid_rel>[-+0-9.eE]+)"
17890 r"(?:\s*\|\s*trial_ratio:\s*(?P<trial_ratio>[-+0-9.eE]+)"
17891 r"(?:\s*\|\s*smoothed_ratio:\s*(?P<smoothed_ratio>[-+0-9.eE]+))?"
17892 r"\s*\|\s*status:\s*(?P<status>\w+)\s*\|\s*dtau_after:\s*(?P<dtau_after>[-+0-9.eE]+)"
17893 r"(?:\s*\|\s*cfl_eff_after:\s*(?P<cfl_eff_after>[-+0-9.eE]+))?)?"
17894 )
17895

17899 for path in sorted(path for pattern in patterns for path in glob.glob(pattern)):
17900 block_match = re.search(r"Block_(\d+)\.log$", path)

17909 continue

17918 "block": block,

18123def _parse_solution_convergence_log(filepath: str) -> "tuple[dict, list[int]]":
18124 """!
18125 @brief Parse solution_convergence.log into latest rows by step plus observed order.
18126
18127 The log format uses pipe-delimited aligned columns. The first line of the
18128 file is a banner (starts with '=') containing the mode tag; the second line
18129 is the column header; the third line is a separator (starts with '-').
18130 Subsequent lines are one data row per timestep.
18131
18132 @param[in] filepath Path to solution_convergence.log.
18133 @return Mapping of step number to a dict of column values.
18134 """
18135 rows_by_step = {}
18136 step_order = []
18137 if not os.path.isfile(filepath):
18138 return rows_by_step, step_order
18139
18140 mode = None
18141 col_names = None
18142
18143 with open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
18144 for raw_line in f:
18145 line = raw_line.strip()
18146 if not line:
18147 continue
18148 if line.startswith("="):
18149 m = re.search(r"\[mode:\s*([\w_]+)", line)
18150 if m:
18151 mode = m.group(1)
18152 continue
18153 if line.startswith("-"):
18154 continue
18155 if col_names is None:
18156 col_names = [p.strip() for p in raw_line.split("|")]
18157 continue
18158 parts = [p.strip() for p in raw_line.split("|")]
18159 if len(parts) < 4 or col_names is None:
18160 continue
18161 step = _parse_int_loose(parts[0]) if col_names[0] == "step" else None
18162 if step is None:
18163 continue
18164 step_order.append(step)
18165 row = {"mode": mode}
18166 for name, val in zip(col_names, parts):
18167 if not name:
18168 continue
18169 float_val = _parse_float_loose(val)
18170 int_val = _parse_int_loose(val)
18171 if float_val is not None and ("." in val or "e" in val.lower()):
18172 row[name] = float_val
18173 elif int_val is not None:
18174 row[name] = int_val
18175 else:
18176 row[name] = val
18177 rows_by_step[step] = row
18178 return rows_by_step, step_order

18181def _find_solver_stream_log_candidates(run_dir: str, log_dir: str) -> "list[str]":

18269 @brief Compute sampled deltas between two particle snapshot samples.

18312 if current_row["rank"] != previous_row["rank"]:
18313 rank_migrations += 1

18316 cell_changes += 1

18323 "rank_migrations": rank_migrations,
18324 "cell_changes": cell_changes,
18325 }

18620def _summary_source_mtime(paths) -> float:
18621 """!
18622 @brief Return the newest modification time among one or more summary sources.
18623 @param[in] paths Path string, iterable of paths, or mapping of paths.
18624 @return Newest modification time, or -1.0 when no source exists.
18625 """
18626 if isinstance(paths, dict):
18627 paths = paths.values()
18628 elif isinstance(paths, str):
18629 paths = [paths]
18630 newest = -1.0
18631 for path in paths or []:
18632 if path and os.path.isfile(path):
18633 newest = max(newest, os.path.getmtime(path))
18634 return newest

18637def _order_summary_step_orders(sources: "list[tuple[list[int], object]]") -> "list[list[int]]":
18638 """!
18639 @brief Order observed step sequences by the recency of their source files.
18640 @param[in] sources Pairs of observed steps and filesystem source path(s).
18641 @return Step-order lists sorted so active append sources are considered first.
18642 """
18643 ranked = []
18644 for priority, (order, paths) in enumerate(sources):
18645 if order:
18646 ranked.append((_summary_source_mtime(paths), priority, order))
18647 ranked.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
18648 return [order for _, _, order in ranked]

19090def _summary_display_value(value) -> str:
19091 """!
19092 @brief Format one configuration-summary value for compact text output.
19093 @param[in] value Value to format.
19094 @return Compact human-readable value.
19095 """
19096 if value is None:
19097 return "-"
19098 if isinstance(value, bool):
19099 return "enabled" if value else "disabled"
19100 if isinstance(value, float):
19101 return f"{value:.6g}"
19102 if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
19103 return ", ".join(_summary_display_value(item) for item in value) if value else "none"
19104 if isinstance(value, dict):
19105 if not value:
19106 return "none"
19107 return ", ".join(f"{key}={_summary_display_value(item)}" for key, item in value.items())
19108 return str(value)

19496def _humanize_plot_identifier(value: str) -> str:
19497 """!
19498 @brief Convert one machine-oriented identifier into a readable plot label.
19499 @param[in] value Dotted path or snake-case identifier.
19500 @return Human-readable label.
19501 """
19502 text = str(value).split(".")[-1].replace("_", " ").strip()
19503 replacements = {
19504 "l2": "L²", "linf": "L∞", "msd": "mean-squared displacement",
19505 "pct": "percentage", "p95": "95th percentile", "cfl": "CFL",
19506 "ke": "kinetic energy", "rms": "RMS",
19507 }
19508 words = [replacements.get(word.lower(), word) for word in text.split()]
19509 return " ".join(words[:1]).capitalize() + (" " + " ".join(words[1:]) if len(words) > 1 else "")

19521def _summary_physical_time(context: dict, record: dict) -> "float | None":

19544 resumed. Rows before the header, or whose width disagrees with it, are skipped rather
19545 than guessed at. `segment` counts the continuations seen so far, so a caller can keep
19546 restarts as separate series instead of drawing a line across the seam.

19891 """!
19892 @brief Collect the per-step scalar histories written by the spectra post stage.
19893
19894 @details Each spectra task keeps its own history file, so one task becomes one
19895 plotted line and several tasks compare directly on the same axes.
19896
19897 @param[in] context Summary context returned by `_build_summary_context()`.
19898 @return Append-ordered plot record list; empty when no spectra were measured.

19903 return records

19905 run_dir, resolve_post_spectra_output_dir(context.get("monitor_cfg") or {})
19906 )
19907 for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(spectra_root):
19908 for filename in sorted(files):

19910 continue
19911 history_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
19912 line = filename[: -len("_history.csv")]
19913 try:
19914 with open(history_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
19915 for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
19916 step = _parse_int_loose(row.get("step"))

19918 continue
19919 values = {}
19920 for column in POST_SPECTRA_SCALAR_COLUMNS:
19921 parsed = _parse_float_loose(row.get(column))
19922 if parsed is not None:
19923 values[column] = parsed
19924 if values:
19925 _append_summary_plot_record(
19926 records, "spectra", step, line, values, history_path, 0,
19927 coordinates={"time": _parse_float_loose(row.get("time"))},
19928 )
19929 except OSError:
19930 # A history a concurrent post stage is still writing is simply not
19931 # listed yet; summarize is read-only and must never fail on it.
19932 continue

19960def _representative_indices(count: int, maximum: int = 6) -> list:
19961 """!
19962 @brief Select evenly distributed indices while always retaining both endpoints.
19963 @param[in] count Number of available ordered states.
19964 @param[in] maximum Maximum states to retain.
19965 @return Sorted unique zero-based indices.
19966 """
19967 if count <= maximum:
19968 return list(range(count))
19969 return sorted({round(index * (count - 1) / (maximum - 1)) for index in range(maximum)})

20103 @param[in] context Summary context returned by `_build_summary_context()`.
20104 @param[in] records Append-ordered plot record list.

20115 if not matching:
20116 raise ValueError(f"Plot series '{series}' is unavailable. Use --list-plot-series to inspect available series.")

20118 for record in matching:
20119 source_path = record["source_path"]
20120 latest_segments[source_path] = max(latest_segments.get(source_path, 0), record.get("segment", 0))
20121 matching = [
20122 record for record in matching

20129 grouped = {}
20130 selected_steps = set()

20133 for record in matching:
20134 iteration = record.get("coordinates", {}).get("solver_iteration")

20136 continue
20137 histories.setdefault((record["source_path"], record["line"]), []).append(record)
20138 for (_source_path, label), history in histories.items():

20148 x_label = "Nonlinear iteration" if source == "momentum" else "Linear iteration"
20149 x_kind = "integer"

tuple picurv_cli.core.staged_control_directories ( str  control_path)

Read run-owned directory values from a staged control file.

Tokenizes with shlex because PETSc's options-file parser treats a double-quoted span as a single token. Splitting on whitespace would read -log_dir "/tmp/VICTIM DIR" as the value "/tmp/VICTIM, which looks relative and contained while PETSc would use the absolute path.

Malformed quoting is reported rather than skipped: a line the parser cannot interpret is exactly the case where preflight must not assume the run is safe.

Parameters
[in]control_pathPath to a generated .control file.
Returns
Tuple of (values, parse_errors).

Definition at line 20645 of file core.py.

20645def staged_control_directories(control_path: str) -> tuple:
20646 """!
20647 @brief Read run-owned directory values from a staged control file.
20648
20649 @details Tokenizes with `shlex` because PETSc's options-file parser treats a
20650 double-quoted span as a single token. Splitting on whitespace would read
20651 `-log_dir "/tmp/VICTIM DIR"` as the value `"/tmp/VICTIM`, which looks
20652 relative and contained while PETSc would use the absolute path.
20653
20654 Malformed quoting is reported rather than skipped: a line the parser
20655 cannot interpret is exactly the case where preflight must not assume the
20656 run is safe.
20657 @param[in] control_path Path to a generated `.control` file.
20658 @return Tuple of (values, parse_errors).
20659 """
20660 flag_to_key = {
20661 "-log_dir": "log",
20662 "-output_dir": "output",
20663 "-restart_dir": "restart",
20664 "-analysis_dir": "analysis",
20665 }
20666 values: dict = {}
20667 parse_errors: list = []
20668 try:
20669 lines = read_text_file_lines(control_path)
20670 except OSError as exc:
20671 return values, [f"could not be read ({exc})"]
20672 for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
20673 if not line.strip():
20674 continue
20675 try:
20676 tokens = shlex.split(line, comments=True)
20677 except ValueError as exc:
20678 parse_errors.append(
20679 f"line {number} has malformed quoting and cannot be interpreted ({exc}); "
20680 f"refusing to assume it is safe"
20681 )
20682 continue
20683 if tokens and tokens[0] in RESERVED_INDIRECTION_FLAGS:
20684 parse_errors.append(
20685 f"line {number} uses '{tokens[0]}', which PETSc expands itself; its contents "
20686 f"cannot be checked here and could set a run directory. Re-stage without it"
20687 )
20688 continue
20689 if len(tokens) >= 2 and tokens[0] in flag_to_key:
20690 values[flag_to_key[tokens[0]]] = tokens[1]
20691 return values, parse_errors
20692
